settings.name_in_paper: contextual MAB problem with stochastic payoffs (similarity space)
unmapped: Expected payoff mu(x,y) is 1-Lipschitz w.r.t. a known similarity metric D on feasible context-arm pairs (compact, diameter <= 1)
only a feasible subset P of X x Y may be playable
settings.definition_quote: In each round t ... a context x_t in X is revealed ..., the algorithm chooses an arm y_t ... (x_t,y_t) in P, payoff pi_t in [0,1] is revealed. The sequence of context arrivals is fixed before the first round ... |mu(x,y) - mu(x',y')| <= D((x,y),(x',y')).

settings.name_in_paper: contextual MAB with stochastic payoffs on a product similarity space (lower bound)
unmapped: product similarity space min(1, D_X + D_Y) known to the learner
settings.definition_quote: Let (P,D) be a product similarity space. Fix an arbitrary time horizon T and a positive number R <= R^UB(T).

settings.name_in_paper: drifting MAB problem (k arms, volatility sigma)
unmapped: expected payoff of each arm changes by at most a known per-round volatility sigma_y (|mu(t,y)-mu(t',y)| <= sigma_y |t-t'|); learner knows the volatility
settings.definition_quote: we assume that expected payoff of each arm y changes by at most sigma_y in each round, for some a-priori known volatilities sigma_y ... We call this setting the drifting MAB problem.

unmapped: similarity D((t,y),(t',y')) = min(1, sigma|t-t'| + D_Y(y,y')) known to learner (known volatility and arms metric)
settings.definition_quote: D((t,y),(t',y')) = min(1, sigma|t-t'| + D_Y(y,y')), where (Y,D_Y) is the arms space.

unmapped: expected payoffs of each arm evolve by independent stochastic processes with uniform [0,1] marginals, satisfying a known per-round volatility bound sigma; regret in expectation over the processes
settings.definition_quote: we assume that expected payoffs mu(.,y) of each arm y evolve over time according to some stochastic process Gamma_y that satisfies (temporal constraint) ... mutually independent, and moreover that the marginal distributions mu(t,y) are uniform on [0,1]

unmapped: expected payoff of each arm is an independent random walk with step +-sigma on [0,1] with reflecting boundaries (1/sigma integer); learner knows sigma; regret in expectation over the walks
settings.definition_quote: Here for each arm y the stochastic process Gamma_y is a random walk with step +- sigma_y. To ensure that the random walk stays within the interval [0,1], we assume reflecting boundaries.

settings.name_in_paper: sleeping MAB problem with stochastic payoffs
unmapped: awake set sequence fixed in advance; regret against best awake arm each round
settings.definition_quote: The sleeping bandits problem is an extension of MAB where in each round some arms can be asleep ... We model sleeping bandits as contextual MAB problem where each context arrival x_t corresponds to the set of arms that are awake in this round.

unmapped: randomized oblivious adversary: per-round payoff-function distributions Pi_t fixed in advance; mu_t Lipschitz on product space (X x Y, D_X + D_Y) and mu*_t Lipschitz on contexts
learner has a context-free bandit subroutine with known convergence time c_Y r^-(2+d_Y) log(1/r) on the instance class
settings.definition_quote: For each round t, there is a payoff function pi_t: X x Y -> [0,1] ... sampled independently from a time-specific distribution Pi_t ... Distributions Pi_t are fixed by the adversary in advance ... adversarial contextual regret R(T) = sum_t mu_t(x_t,y_t) - mu*_t(x_t)

source.label: thm:ZoomAlg
source.quote: Consider the contextual MAB problem with stochastic payoffs. There is an algorithm (namely, Algorithm~\ref{alg:contextual-zooming} described below) whose contextual regret $R(T)$ satisfies~\refeq{eq:regret-covNum} with $N_r$ equal to $N_r(\mPzoom)$, the $r$-zooming number. Consequently, $R(T)$ satisfies the dimension-type guarantee~\refeq{eq:regret-dim}, where $d_c$ is the \ZoomDim.

results.notes: Also gives N_r-type bound C_0 inf_{r0}(r0 T + sum_{r=2^-i>=r0} N_r log T / r) with N_r the r-zooming number; recorded only the dimension-type form. Pessimistically d_c is the covering dimension of the similarity space. Expectation type not explicitly stated; regret defined through means.

symbols.c_mult: multiplier c in covering-type dimension (any c>0)

source.label: thm:ZoomAlg-adjusted
source.quote: Consider the contextual MAB problem with stochastic payoffs. The contextual regret $R(T)$ of the contextual zooming algorithm satisfies~\refeq{eq:regret-covNum}, where $N_r$ is the adjusted $r$-zooming number and $C_0$ is the doubling constant of the similarity space times some absolute constant. Consequently, $R(T)$ satisfies the dimension-type guarantee~\refeq{eq:regret-dim}, where $d_c$ is the corresponding covering-type dimension.

results.notes: No proof given (sketch omitted). Dimension-type form recorded; N_r-type form also stated.

conditions: regret in expectation over a distribution I of instances on which the instance-dependent upper bound R^UB_mu(T) <= O(R)

source.label: thm:LBs-strong
source.quote: Consider the contextual MAB problem with stochastic payoffs, Let $(\mP,\D)$ be a product similarity space. Fix an arbitrary time horizon $T$ and a positive number $R\leq \regretUB(T)$. Then there exists a distribution $\mI$ over problem instances on $(\mP,\D)$ with the following two properties: (a) $\regretUB_{\mu}(T) \leq O(R)$ for each problem instance in support(I). (b) for any contextual bandit algorithm it holds that $\E_{\mI}[R(T)] \geq \Omega(R/\log T)$

results.notes: Derived from Lemma 5.2: at T_0 = N r^-2, E_I[R(T_0)] >= Omega(N/r) while R^UB_mu(T_0) <= O(N/r) log T_0.

symbols.sigma_vol: per-round volatility (max change of each arm's expected payoff per round), sigma_y = sigma for all arms

conditions: all arms have equal volatility sigma (paper notes it extends to the average volatility)

source.label: cor:driftingMAB-pessimistic
source.quote: Consider the drifting MAB problem with $k$ arms and volatilities $\sigma_y\equiv \sigma$. Contextual zooming with period $T_0$ has average dynamic regret $\hat{R}(T) = O(k\sigma \log T_0)^{1/3}$, whenever $T\geq T_0\geq (\tfrac{k}{\sigma^2})^{1/3}\, \log \tfrac{k}{\sigma} $.

results.notes: Paper bounds average dynamic regret R(T)/T; multiplied by T. Paper says it is optimal up to log factors (details omitted).

symbols.d_Y: covering dimension of the arms space
symbols.c_mult: multiplier k of the covering dimension of the arms space

source.quote: Consider the drifting MAB problem with spatial constraints~\refeq{eq:driftingMAB-spatial}, where $\sigma$ is the volatility. Let $d$ be the covering dimension of the arms space, with multiplier $k$. Contextual zooming with period $T_0$ has average dynamic regret $\hat{R}(T) = O(k\, \sigma \log T_0)^{\tfrac{1}{d+3}}$, whenever ...

results.notes: Average regret multiplied by T. Paper's k here is the covering multiplier, not the number of arms.

conditions: expectation over independent payoff processes with uniform marginals

source.label: cor:driftingMAB-marginals
source.quote: Consider drifting MAB with uniform marginals, with $k$ arms and volatilities $\sigma_y\equiv \sigma$. Contextual zooming with period $T_0$ satisfies $\E_\Gamma[\hat{R}(T)] = O(k\,\sigma^{2/3}\,\log T_0)$, whenever $T\geq T_0\geq \sigma^{-2/3} \log\tfrac{1}{\sigma}$.

results.notes: Average regret multiplied by T; expectation over the payoff processes Gamma.

tuning: similarity D_{T_0}((t,y),(t',y')) = min(1, sigma|t-t'|^{1/2} log T_0 + 1{y != y'})

source.label: cor:DynamicMAB
source.quote: Consider the Dynamic MAB problem with $k$ arms and volatilities $\sigma_y\equiv \sigma$. Let $\mathtt{ALG}_{T_0}$ denote the contextual zooming algorotihm with period $T_0$ which is parameterized by the similarity space $(\mP,\D_{T_0})$. Then $\mathtt{ALG}_{T_0}$ satisfies $\E_\Gamma[\hat{R}(T)] = O(k\,\sigma\,\log^2 T_0)$, whenever $T\geq T_0\geq \tfrac{1}{\sigma} \log\tfrac{1}{\sigma}$.

results.notes: Average regret multiplied by T. Matches Slivkins & Upfal (2008).

bound.regime: for any r_0 > 0, sum restricted to arms with Delta_cons_i > r_0

symbols.Delta_cons_i: gap between consecutive sorted means, mu_{i+1} - mu_i (arms sorted increasingly)
symbols.r_0: free threshold r > 0 (infimum taken over it)

conditions: sum over arms i with Delta_cons_i > r_0 only

source.quote: Consider the sleeping MAB problem with stochastic payoffs. Order the arms so that their expected payoffs are $\mu_1\leq \mu_2 \leq \ldots \leq \mu_n$, where $n$ is the number of arms. Let $\Delta_i = \mu_{i+1}-\mu_i$. Then $R(T) \leq \inf_{r>0} ( rT + \sum_{i:\, \Delta_i>r}\; \frac{O(\log T)}{\Delta_i} )$.

results.notes: Delta_i here is consecutive-mean gap, not the standard gap. Restricted sum not expressible in SymPy; condition recorded. Recovers Kleinberg et al. (2008).
